deficiencies.sourcePassage: Neuroectodermal tumors are the ones that kind of deviate from the nomenclature system.

considerations.sourcePassage: Okay? So just so that we're all on the same page in terms of nomenclature, and of course, with any naming system, there are always exceptions to every rule.
considerations.reason: The audience-directed introduction is appropriately omitted, while the substantive point that naming systems have exceptions is retained.

considerations.sourcePassage: But the general way in which things are thought about, if you like, in terms of benign tumors, is that you have the name of the tissue plus oma, which are things like lipoma, leiomyoma, papilloma, and adenomas. All of these would be benign tumors in the tissues that they are occurring in. So the fat, smooth muscle or papillomas in the skin, and adenomas, as we were talking about in the colon.
considerations.reason: The rewrite faithfully preserves the general naming rule, the examples, their benign status and the indicated tissue associations. Expanding the elliptical list into complete textbook prose does not change its meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: So malignant tumors, on the other hand, of the epithelium, and the mesenchyme have things like carcinoma and sarcoma attached to them as suffixes. And so you have breast carcinomas or colorectal adenocarcinomas and osteosarcomas and leiomyosarcomas. So that's the general rule of thumb for those. So by the time you have these suffixes, this would be a malignant disease.
considerations.reason: The rewrite retains the suffixes, all four examples, the rule-of-thumb qualification and the statement that these suffixes denote malignant disease.

considerations.sourcePassage: Within the hematopoietic system, you have leukemias, which are, of course, the liquid circulating neoplasms within the body, and also the lymphomas, which would be solid within the lymph nodes, within those structures.
considerations.reason: The distinction between circulating leukaemias and solid lymphomas in lymph nodes is preserved; only conversational phrasing is removed.

considerations.sourcePassage: So you have cells, these are tumors that derive from the cells that form the central and peripheral nervous system. So you have names like glioma and glioblastoma and neuroblastoma. These are all, even though they have oma in them, these are all malignant tumors, and things like retinoblastoma.
considerations.reason: The rewrite preserves the cellular origin, the examples, the presence of -oma in their names and their malignant status. The false start “So you have cells” is appropriately removed.

considerations.sourcePassage: So these are these different tumor types and other exceptions as well, things like malignant melanoma. Melanoma is never used for moles, for example. This always denotes a malignant status.
considerations.reason: The rewrite faithfully retains malignant melanoma as another exception and the statements that melanoma is not used for moles and always denotes malignancy.
